assumptions: The product remains a workflow and control layer and never charges for, or represents ownership of, the legally free registry or VoP result.
Any bank-provided VoP evidence is processed only when a host has explicit contractual rights to pass, retain, and export it; the product receives no direct EPC access.
A useful first version can operate on registry checks, change freezes, remediation, dual approval, and audit evidence even when reusable VoP evidence is unavailable.
No platform commitment, price acceptance, activation rate, renewal behavior, data-sharing right, or positive unit economics is assumed beyond the supplied evidence.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid, scoped pilot or binding conditional agreement with a Polish accounting or AP platform that specifies distribution, data rights, implementation effort, security obligations, and commercial terms, followed by measured activation, supplier completion, false-match, exception-labor, retention, and contribution-margin results.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly identifies the supplier-change gate as the control point and separates a chargeable remediation and audit workflow from free registry and bank checks. Consolidating access and distribution in the host is coherent, although it concentrates the opportunity around one unproven relationship.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Supplier impersonation and fraudulent account changes are credible, high-consequence problems, and incumbent paid products show category-level willingness to pay. Evidence does not yet show that Polish accounting or AP platforms experience enough attributable pain, can monetize the control, or prefer an external OEM module.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: An annual OEM minimum plus portfolio-linked usage could create recurring revenue and amortize one integration across many entities. Pricing, activation, sales-cycle cost, revenue share, implementation burden, support, security, liability, renewal, and contribution margin are all unresolved, while partner-specific work could consume the apparent software leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish accounting and AP platforms form a specific beachhead with a clear workflow trigger and potential portfolio reach. The packet provides no buyer count, reachable portfolio volume, event frequency, budget ownership, or evidence that this narrow segment alone is economically meaningful.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local registry knowledge, white-label delivery, and focus on the host workflow may support a focused wedge. SurePay and Trustpair already cover overlapping controls, while banks, ERPs, or the target platform can bundle or build the function; no exclusive access, channel lock, or superior performance is established.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful supplier-change control can plausibly extend into onboarding, continuous master-data monitoring, payment approval, additional platform portfolios, and other jurisdictions. Expansion would require new registry, bank, legal, language, and integration work, so success in one Polish host would not automatically transfer.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded approval history, resolved-name rules, integration depth, and workflow switching costs could compound. Those benefits depend on uncertain retention and cross-tenant data rights, and the core registry input is public, VoP is free and access-constrained, and the surrounding workflow is reproducible by better-distributed incumbents or hosts.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A localized, embedded freeze-remediate-approve packet could be more convenient than disconnected checks and could reduce operational gaps. No evidence quantifies fraud reduction, labor savings, accuracy, deployment speed, price advantage, or user preference relative to incumbent, bank, ERP, or in-house alternatives.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The 2027 Polish VoP timetable and recognized BEC risk create a timely reason to revisit supplier controls. The same regulation makes the name check free at the PSP and may let banks or platforms absorb the surrounding workflow, so timing raises both awareness and substitution pressure.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: One host contract could distribute the module across a portfolio and avoid costly entity-by-entity selling. There is no committed design partner or evidence for access to platform buyers, sales-cycle length, integration priority, activation, revenue share, or repeatability, making the proposed leverage a single critical dependency rather than a demonstrated channel.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The registry-first prototype suits the founder's technical skills, capital, and part-time constraint, and the staged scope avoids custody and direct EPC access. Enterprise procurement, security, tenant isolation, data rights, professional liability, bank-specific interfaces, and concentrated platform integration may exceed the available time and budget before commercial proof.

highest_value_structural_change: Decouple economic proof from a full OEM deployment by making the first offer a low-integration, paid shadow-mode pilot for one portfolio operator, with registry, remediation, approval, and audit value that works without reusable VoP; require measured use and explicit data rights before undertaking production platform integration.
main_structural_strength: Embedding prevention at the host's supplier-change and payment gate can amortize one control integration across a managed-company portfolio while monetizing workflow and evidence rather than the free underlying checks.
primary_score_limiter: The same uncommitted platform relationship must supply the payer, distribution, integration surface, and any VoP or learning rights, leaving the channel, economics, and prospective moat jointly unresolved.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The EPC interface is restricted to inter-PSP communication, Nordea illustrates that a corporate API may expose VoP only inside payment initiation, and both the mandated VoP check and Polish registry lookup are free, sharply limiting proprietary access and standalone pricing power.
